messages:
Maya (CSM): Quick sync — we need to finalize the onboarding SLA/SLO dashboard + credit runbook for the new accounts going live this week. Acme wants 99.9% uptime and p99 latency < 300ms for text generation. Who can help consolidate definitions + examples for CS?
Liam (CSE): I can grab the dashboard widgets and tidy labels. Do we have a canonical definition for uptime here (5xx/errors vs node down)?
Diego (SRE): For our infra we compute availability as 1 - (total_errors/total_requests) over the period. Total_errors = 5xx + request timeouts. That aligns with how credits are triggered.
Liam (CSE): ok — will standardize labels to: availability, p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms), request rate.
Ashley (PM): Need an email template for customers explaining credits and when they apply. Also want the CS playbook steps when SLO breaches occur.
Maya (CSM): High level runbook idea: 1) Confirm metrics on dashboard 2) Notify customer 3) Calculate credit 4) Apply credit/review with finance. We need formulas.
Diego (SRE): Credit calc we used in pilot: credit_percentage = min( (SLO_target - measured_availability) / SLO_target, 1.0 ) * 100. Example: target 99.9, measured 99.5 => ((99.9-99.5)/99.9)*100 ~= 0.4% invoice credit. I'll paste the PromQL snippet I'm using for availability: ```
availability = 1 - sum(increase(inference_http_requests_total{job="inference",status=~"5.."}[1h])) / sum(increase(inference_http_requests_total{job="inference"}[1h]))
```
Liam (CSE): Nice. I'll convert that to a grafana query and add a p99 panel (query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))).
Maya (CSM): For customer messaging: keep it simple — "We monitor availability and latency against your SLA. If availability drops below 99.9% during the billing period, we calculate a proportionate credit. See attached dashboard link."
Ashley (PM): Can someone draft the exact wording + example calculations for the customer-facing doc? Also need the internal CS runbook steps with who to CC (finance, legal for >X% credit).
Liam (CSE): I'll draft the internal runbook snippet and the grafana dashboard annotations. Will add example calculations with three scenarios (minor drop, sustained outage, p99 latency breach).
Maya (CSM): Assignments: @Liam — dashboard + runbook draft by EOD tomorrow. @Diego — confirm the PromQL and define the alert thresholds for auto-notify (suggest: availability < 99.9% for 5m and sustained < 99.7% for 1h). @Ashley — customer email template and escalation doc. I'll compile final playbook and send to Acme.
Diego (SRE): Ack. I'll also add a note about partial region outages and model fallback — we need to be explicit about when fallback counts as degraded vs unavailable.
OpsBot: Incident created: INC-20260307-457 — SLO reporting runbook review. Assigned to Liam, Diego, Ashley.
Maya (CSM): One more ask — can we add a small "how we measure latency" blurb: p99 measured from request ingress to last token produced; excludes client-side batching. Liam do you want to add a tiny diagram?
Liam (CSE): Yep, will add a diagram and a short FAQ entry: "Why does my p99 differ from my client logs?"
Ashley (PM): Target timeline: draft by tomorrow EOD, internal review day after, customer-facing doc by end of week. Sound good?
Diego (SRE): Sounds good. I'll PR the PromQL and alert rules today.
Maya (CSM): Great — thanks everyone. I'll schedule a 20m follow-up Friday to sign off before we send to Acme.
Liam (CSE): :thumbsup:
Ashley (PM): :+1:
Maya (CSM): Thanks — will post the finalized doc in this thread when ready.
OpsBot: Reminder set for 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC: SLA playbook sync.
